title: Adaptive Delta Detector for Region Routing with Staged Variant Escrow
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight, adaptive detector that identifies when inter-region latency distributions exhibit a widening p50->p95 delta and combine that signal with network-quality heuristics (packet loss, TCP retransmit rate, recent connection failures) to drive region selection and staged fallback to compatible model variants.

Motivation: current region selection primarily uses percentile scoring but lacks a tunable mechanism to detect distribution shape changes that predict near-term tail degradation. By explicitly tracking the delta between p50 and p95 and cross-correlating it with short-lived network anomalies, we can proactively shift traffic to healthier regions or route to lower-cost variants before user-facing errors spike.

High-level design:
- Delta detector: per-POP and per-route EWMA of p50 and p95 with a configurable smoothing window (default 2m). Compute delta = p95 - p50 and a normalized delta_ratio = delta / max(p50, 1ms). Raise a delta_alert when delta_ratio exceeds threshold T_dynamic. Threshold adapts based on recent variance (T_dynamic = base_T * (1 + 0.5*variance_ratio)).
- Network health fusion: ingest packet_loss (last 1m), conn_fail_rate, and retransmit_rate, normalize to 0..1, compute network_penalty = max(packet_loss_norm, conn_fail_norm) * weight_net + retransmit_norm * weight_ret.
- Composite score: score = base_latency_percentile_score + alpha * delta_penalty + beta * network_penalty. delta_penalty scales with delta_ratio and recent trend slope.
- Staged variant escrow: when composite score crosses soft_threshold, mark region as "escrowed" for that route and begin canary shift (5% traffic) to a fallback model variant (quantized / smaller context). If score remains above hard_threshold or error rate increases, escalate to 25% then 100% failover. Escrow state keeps a small prefetched KV cache for quick revert and records metrics for rollback decisioning.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- False positives: overly sensitive delta detection may cause unnecessary variant churn. Mitigation: require sustained delta alerts for two consecutive EWMA windows and verify corroborating network_penalty before canary.
- Cost: prefetched KV caches and canary traffic increase expense. Limit prefetched cache size by LRU window and use eviction TTL tied to escrow state.
- Cross-POP correlation: avoid oscillation by applying a global hysteresis window and minimum hold time for escrow states (default 3 minutes).

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics emitted per-route/per-pop: p50_ewma_ms, p95_ewma_ms, delta_ratio, delta_trend_slope, network_penalty, composite_score, escrow_state, canary_pct, fallback_variant_id.
- Dashboards: a per-route "Delta Guard" panel showing delta_ratio heatmap across POPs, current escrowed regions, and active canaries. Add alert rules for composite_score > hard_threshold for more than 2m.

Acceptance criteria:
- Detector produces delta_ratio and composite_score with <10ms added processing latency per request path when enabled.
- Simulated incident test (see testing_plan) results in failover to fallback variant within 3 minutes for pax0-like faults and within 90s for severe packet loss scenarios.
- No oscillation in region selection for at least 15m in the post-rollback soak tests.

Next steps:
- Implement detection kernel in routing service (phase 1) and add feature flag behind route-level toggle.
- Build staged-escrow state machine in orchestrator and integrate with variant router.
- Create e2e test scenarios in sim harness and replay against recent telemetry.

Notes from initial spike:
- Local simulation of synthetic tail events shows delta_ratio threshold of 1.8 (p95 nearly double p50) gives 92% precision for predicting request timeouts in 2m window.
- Team review (2026-03-04): PM prefers conservative defaults to avoid customer-visible variant churn. Design adjusted to require both delta and network_penalty corroboration.
- Security: no new data plane secrets; escrow caches respect existing KMS-backed encryption at rest.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Spike complete: built EWMA-based delta detector prototype and synthetic load test (Ava). Key finding: delta ratio triggers earlier than raw p95 threshold for simulated link flaps.
2026-03-04 - Design review (Ravi, Mei, Carlos): asked to add global hysteresis and minimum hold time to prevent oscillation. Agreed on staged canary 5%->25%->100% and prefetched KV escrow idea.
2026-03-06 - Implementation note: started routing-service branch eng-100045/delta-detector. Added feature flag routing.delta_detector.enabled. (Ravi)
2026-03-08 - QA: created sim scenarios for asymmetric tail increases and churning pop health. Found one bug: composite_score not reset after network transient; fix pending in PR.
2026-03-10 - PM feedback (Mei Chen): prefer default base_T higher (less sensitive). Updated thresholds and added require-sustained rule in description.
acceptance_criteria: Emitter metrics for p50_ewma_ms, p95_ewma_ms, delta_ratio, composite_score available for all routes when enabled
Feature flag toggle enables detector without restart and with <10ms per-request overhead
Canary shift completes according to staged percentages and reverts cleanly on rollback
Simulated scenarios reproduce expected failover timing (<3 minutes)
testing_plan: Unit tests for delta calculation and adaptive threshold logic
Integration test: enable delta_detector on staging route + inject synthetic tail latency on pop-A -> expect canary to pop-B at 5% then escalate
Chaos test: produce brief packet loss spikes and validate detector requires corroborating network_penalty before acting
Soak test: run for 2h against production-shaped trace replay to detect oscillation
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind route toggle, internal-only on perf/staging routes
Phase 1: Canary on <10 high-traffic routes with detailed dashboards and on-call runbook
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to all routes after 1 week with no false-positive >3 per route
Rollback: immediately flip flag and promote cached KV to restore hot-path for affected users
